agents.name: Irinotecan
agents.mechanism: Interferes with repair of genetic-material breaks
agents.explanation: Irinotecan blocks topoisomerase I, an enzyme involved in handling deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material. Cancer-cell division is disrupted. Blood and bowel cells are also affected. Early infusion-related bowel symptoms and later diarrhoea need different treatment plans.
visual: Blood and bowel cells can be affected
Early and delayed diarrhoea need different actions
agents.watch: Tell staff about cramping, sweating, runny eyes/nose or diarrhoea during or soon after infusion. Later watery stools require the prescribed diarrhoea plan and immediate oncology contact. Fever, dizziness, reduced urine, severe abdominal pain or inability to drink needs urgent assessment.
risks: Delayed diarrhoea that can be severe or life-threatening, causing dehydration, electrolyte loss or kidney injury
Early cholinergic symptoms such as sweating, abdominal cramps and diarrhoea during or shortly after infusion
Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; diarrhoea with low counts is especially hazardous
Nausea, vomiting, mouth soreness, appetite loss, fatigue and hair loss
Severe allergic reactions and uncommon serious lung inflammation
Fertility effects and pregnancy harm; medicine interactions can increase toxicity

agents.name: Temozolomide
agents.mechanism: Adds chemical damage to genetic material
agents.explanation: The body converts temozolomide into an active substance that damages deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material, interrupting cell division. Although taken as capsules, it can cause serious blood, liver and infection problems and requires the prescribed checks.
visual: Blood, liver and infection checks continue
agents.watch: Report fever, new cough or breathlessness, unusual bleeding, jaundice, severe rash or persistent vomiting urgently. Take capsules exactly as prescribed; do not replace a dose after vomiting. Follow the infection-prevention prescription and report any missed doses to the team.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; prolonged marrow failure can occur
Opportunistic infections, including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and reactivation of hepatitis B or other infections
Liver injury, including liver failure, which can occur after treatment has finished
Nausea, vomiting, appetite/bowel changes, fatigue, headache, rash and hair effects
Severe allergic or blistering skin reactions and lung inflammation
Later bone-marrow disorders or blood cancers, fertility effects and pregnancy harm

anatomy: Report mouth sores or trouble drinking early. Use the prescribed mouth-care and anti-sickness plan.
New cough or breathlessness needs urgent assessment. Take the prescribed infection-prevention medicine.
Blood tests check liver effects. Yellow eyes, dark urine or significant upper abdominal pain needs prompt advice.
Diarrhoea or vomiting can cause dehydration. Very little urine, dizziness or inability to drink needs urgent help.
Report diarrhoea immediately and follow the written plan. Severe pain, fever or persistent vomiting needs urgent help.
Fever, shaking chills, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs immediate oncology contact.
Report rash and line-site pain early. Blistering or peeling skin or sores involving the eyes needs urgent assessment.
Fatigue and dizziness can affect daily tasks. Sudden confusion, collapse or seizures needs emergency assessment.

monitoring_schedule.note: Safety monitoring is separate from scans and tumour-response review. The exact sequence can change after toxicity or local treatment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect infection, anaemia and bleeding risks from both medicines.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle. Current irinotecan product information recommends weekly blood counts during treatment; the team gives exact sampling dates and any additional tests.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney function and hydration
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify dehydration and impaired clearance during bowel illness.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; urgent extra tests may be needed during diarrhoea, vomiting, reduced urine or poor intake.

monitoring_test_details.label: Liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect liver injury and guide safe dosing.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle, plus after every treatment cycle, including the final cycle, as required by temozolomide product information. Further tests follow symptoms or abnormal results. Liver toxicity can appear weeks or more after the last treatment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Hepatitis B screening and follow-up
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify infection that can reactivate during treatment.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Screen before treatment. Positive results require expert review and a monitoring/prevention plan during and after treatment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Bowel function and infection review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Distinguish acute irinotecan reactions from delayed diarrhoea and recognise infection.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Review before treatment and before restarting after a hold. Record the worst diarrhoea, recovery date, fever, oral intake and urine output; contact oncology promptly when symptoms begin.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour response and local-treatment review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess benefit separately from treatment safety.
monitoring_test_details.timing: The specialist sets scans and clinical reviews according to tumour type, disease extent, symptoms and any surgery or radiotherapy plan.

support.title: Anti-sickness medicines
support.text: Follow one written prevention, home and rescue plan. The team reconciles all steroids and interacting medicines; no generic reference is an additional prescription.

support.title: Infection prevention
support.text: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prevention is required with this temozolomide regimen. The prescribed medicine helps prevent an opportunistic lung infection; follow its full course and report new cough or breathlessness. Hepatitis B results may require a separate expert prevention and follow-up plan.

support.title: Acute irinotecan reactions
support.text: Sweating, cramps and early diarrhoea during or soon after infusion can be a cholinergic reaction. Tell the nurse immediately. The national regimen says atropine should not be used in patients with glaucoma. Tell the treatment team if you have glaucoma. This source does not give a fixed atropine dose.

support.title: Delayed diarrhoea plan
support.text: Irinotecan can cause two different bowel problems. Cramping, sweating and diarrhoea during or shortly after infusion can be an acute cholinergic reaction: tell the nurse immediately; prescribed atropine may be used. Delayed diarrhoea begins more than 24 hours later and can cause dangerous dehydration or infection. Contact oncology at the first loose stool and follow the written anti-diarrhoeal and rehydration prescription. Fever, severe pain, blood, faintness, very little urine or inability to drink needs immediate assessment; never wait for a time threshold when seriously unwell.

support.title: Capsules and missed or vomited doses
support.text: If a temozolomide dose is missed, contact the treatment team for instructions. Never double a dose or restart a held course yourself. If vomiting occurs after temozolomide, do not take an extra dose. Capsules must be swallowed whole, fasting, at least one hour before irinotecan.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The treatment service chooses suitable intravenous access. Report burning, pain, swelling or redness during administration immediately. If a port or central catheter is used, agree dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Do not alter infusion settings yourself. Keep temozolomide in its supplied packaging; do not crush or open capsules. Ask the pharmacy how carers should handle the medicine and what to do after a damaged capsule or spill.

support.title: Fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment; these combinations can permanently affect fertility. Obtain a written pregnancy-prevention, contraception and breastfeeding plan covering every medicine and the longest relevant precaution period. Current product instructions differ from the older general six-month regimen paragraph. Do not assume one interval applies to everyone, and contact oncology promptly if pregnancy is possible.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: The specialist sarcoma team reviews prior treatments, disease sites, symptoms, available further systemic options and suitable clinical trials. Selected surgery or radiotherapy may help local control or symptoms; it is not automatically part of this capsule/infusion calendar. Symptom-focused treatment, rehabilitation and supportive or palliative care remain options alongside or instead of further chemotherapy.

items.text: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste changes, diarrhoea or constipation; fatigue, hair, nail and skin changes; changes in sexual wellbeing; allergic reactions and intravenous-line complications; blood clots, including clots in the legs or lungs; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. evidence.title: rEECur interim irinotecan/temozolomide report and adult-containing retrospective Ewing series
evidence.summary: Prospective interim trial evidence and retrospective studies show activity in some relapsed Ewing sarcomas. In the rEECur comparison, the irinotecan/temozolomide arm was less effective than the other then-open arms and was closed. The existence of responses does not establish superiority or an individual chance of benefit.
evidence.intro: Prospective interim trial evidence and retrospective studies show activity in some relapsed Ewing sarcomas. In the rEECur comparison, the irinotecan/temozolomide arm was less effective than the other then-open arms and was closed. The existence of responses does not establish superiority or an individual chance of benefit.
evidence.caveat: The rEECur figures are from an interim conference report, not a completed full-paper comparison. Retrospective series are subject to selection bias; the adult-containing Palmerini series used irinotecan 40 mg/m², not this national 50 mg/m² schedule. Disease control includes stable disease and must not be labelled response.
evidence.interpretation: The rEECur figures are from an interim conference report, not a completed full-paper comparison. questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: Can I restart after symptoms improve?
questions.a: Only after the treating team confirms the new prescription. A normal test or recovered symptom does not erase previous severe toxicity or a permanent-stop decision.

source_provenance.basis: Current official extracted regimen text and specifically retained primary evidence. No original National Cancer Control Programme PDF binary or source-table pixel verification claimed.
source_provenance.clinical_draft_status: Candidate input; independent source challenge still in progress. Final clinical hashes must be pinned before integration.

general: These reusable agent sections do not decide dose, phase, eligibility, prophylaxis or treatment duration. The parent author supplies current National Cancer Control Programme regimen sources and schedule-specific instructions.
No adverse-event percentages are invented or transferred from another cancer population. Generic risks must remain alongside all selected agent sections.
Clinical source hash freeze remains pending. No independent clinical/pharmacy approval, original-PDF binary verification or fresh visual-table review is claimed.
Contraception and breastfeeding instructions must be reconciled across every selected agent and the actual supplied products; do not use the older generic six-month interval as a universal rule.
dactinomycin: Current detailed safety source is the UK manufacturer SmPC, text revision 3 September 2025, EMC update 16 September 2025. It is not proof of current Irish product authorisation or supply.

Historical Irish PA1301/003/001 listing, https://www.hpra.ie/find-a-medicine/for-human-use/authorised-medicines/details/26050, records withdrawal on 1 April 2012 while also displaying Marketed. The old 2011 linked SmPC must not be labelled current Irish information.

This historical licence status does not mean the current National Cancer Control Programme regimen has been withdrawn. Pharmacy must confirm the supplied product and the applicable authorisation/unlicensed-supply arrangements.

UK product advice gives contraception during treatment and at least seven months afterwards for women/four months for men; no breastfeeding. These are agent-specific facts, not an automatically final combined-regimen interval.
cyclophosphamide: Current Irish source is explicitly Cyclophosphamide Seacross 500 mg, revision 7 January 2026; do not silently call it Endoxana or use the older UK Baxter 2016 text as current Irish evidence.
Ewing sarcoma is among the product indications; this does not establish that every tumour or combination in the National Cancer Control Programme source is licensed.
Product renal advice differs from National Cancer Control Programme IE/VAC. No numeric product dose adjustment is imported into patient definitions.
This product states contraception for six months after treatment for women/three months for men; breastfeeding is contraindicated. Reconcile all selected medicines.
vincristine: Current Irish product revision August 2026 specifies female contraception during and at least seven months after treatment; male contraception during and at least four months afterwards; breastfeeding avoidance during and for one month afterwards. Apply the reconciled combined-regimen plan.
CYP3A4/azole interactions can amplify neurotoxicity. The regimen's constipation and interaction plan must accompany the nerve-risk section.
Do not equate vincristine's blood-count effects with the principal marrow toxicity of the whole combination or copy incidence from other combinations.
doxorubicin: The retained HPRA example product was listed as authorised but not marketed when checked; confirm the actual supplied formulation. Conventional doxorubicin must not be substituted with a liposomal formulation.
Temporary red colour does not justify dismissing haematuria in an ifosfamide/cyclophosphamide combination. Lifetime exposure and regimen-specific ceilings remain professional planning issues.
irinotecan: Current October 2025 HPRA retained text supports delayed diarrhoea, weekly blood counts and liver monitoring. A fresh focused fetch was inaccessible; older Irish product text is explicitly supplementary for cholinergic/lung warnings, not dosing.

Early cholinergic symptoms and delayed diarrhoea are separate. Atropine glaucoma precautions and the prescribed loperamide/escalation plan belong in regimen support; no adult self-dosing schedule is supplied here.
Do not import colorectal doses, paediatric eligibility or numerical adverse-event rates into the sarcoma combinations.
temozolomide: EMA index lists product information updated 18 August 2026. One direct PDF attempt returned HTTP 429; no identical retry was made. Indexed official safety sections and readable manufacturer text were used; full latest-table inspection is not claimed.
Do not transfer glioma/radiotherapy seizure or neurological event rates, glioma dosing, or a 42-day radiotherapy monitoring calendar to these sarcoma regimens.

The National Cancer Control Programme 00504 and 00757 sources themselves require Pneumocystis prophylaxis: this is not an extrapolated requirement based only on the brain-radiotherapy product schedule.
The current product recommends liver tests after each cycle and warns of delayed hepatotoxicity. Baseline-only or pre-cycle-only wording would be incomplete.
